Powered By Apptegy Visit us to learn more About Us School District #37 was created as a small district to save the village of Gretna in 1888. The first school to serve Gretna children was located across the road from the LaBorde cemetery outside Gretna. A two-story brick schoolhouse was constructed in 1898 south of Angus Street across from St. Patrick's Catholic Church. Its size was doubled in 1908, and a gymnasium was added in 1936. As the village grew, so too did the school district. Through minor consolidation over the years and a major consolidation in 1958, the district has grown to its present size of 86 square miles. Centrally located between Lincoln and Omaha, the community uniquely weaves its large city ties with rural character. These appealing characteristics draw many families hoping to raise their children in a small town atmosphere with a sense of community. Mission The Mission of Gretna Public Schools is to accept all students unconditionally and maximize their potential. Philosophy The philosophy of the Gretna Public School System is to provide an equal educational process in relation to the characteristics and needs of the individual student and the community this school serves. The purpose of the school are to challenge the student to discover, develop, and supply knowledge in a changing, complex society and to extend learning experiences designed to motivate individual creativeness and develop a positive self image. Thus, the Gretna Public School System will seek to accomplish these purposes through the commitment and involvement of every person in the community. To develop a positive educational environment that accepts all students and emphasizes their intellectual, physical, emotional and social development. To adopt financial policies that ensure quality educational facilities, equipment, and materials to aid in the accomplishment of the districtÊ¼s educational goals. To attract and retain highly qualified personnel and promote opportunities for their professional growth and development. To develop studentsÊ¼ knowledge and values so they will be effective participants in our democratic society. To develop academic skills in the areas of reading, writing, computing, listening, and speaking so students may effectively interact in our society. To provide opportunities for students to gain an appreciation for the fine and performing arts. To provide educational programs, which allow students to identify and achieve their career goals and emphasize the value of hard work. To introduce students to a variety of activities which encourage them to develop morally, physically, socially, academically, emotionally and spiritually. Community Report The Community Reports include informative data compiled for the families and patrons of the Gretna Public Schools as well as the general public. This report has been prepared to provide a âsnapshotâ of our school system. Community Reports External Visit Gretna Public Schools recently hosted a team of 17 Nebraska educational leaders who visited every school in the district as part of an external review. The team praised our strong curriculum, engaging classrooms, supportive staff, and welcoming school culture, while providing recommendations to help us continue growing and improving for every student. Powered By Apptegy Visit us to learn more Strategic Plan For the first time in our districtâs history, Gretna Public Schools has developed a comprehensive Strategic Plan to guide our future. Since April 2024, we have worked alongside Kordica Communication to facilitate discussions, organize focus groups, and gather valuable input from a diverse range of stakeholdersâincluding students, teachers, classified staff, administrators, parents, Citizens Committee members, city officials, school board members, and local business owners. Through this collaborative effort, we identified four key focus areas that will shape our districtâs priorities from 2025 to 2029 : Curriculum, Instruction, and Assessment Growth, Climate, and Culture Mental Health Recruitment and Retention These four focus areas serve as the foundation of our plan, providing a roadmap for continuous improvement, stakeholder engagement, and aligned district actions. Together, we are committed to ensuring a strong and successful future for Gretna Public Schools. 
   View Plan
 Curriculum, Instruction and Assessment GOAL All students will maximize their individual growth through engaging curriculum and strategic instructional goals. 
   View Plan
 Growth/Climate and Culture GOAL As the district grows, we will address facility needs and nurture a culture that honors the past, celebrates the present and builds a safe and welcoming future for all. 
   View Plan
 Mental Health GOAL All students will learn in a culture that recognizes and responds to their social-emotional, behavioral and overall mental health needs. 
   View Plan
 Recruit and Retain GOAL Gretna Public Schools will recruit and retain highly qualified and caring staff who live the districtâs mission. 
   View Plan

 Supporting Our Strategic Plan Goal Growth / Climate and Culture As our district grows, we are committed to more than just buildings and enrollment. We are focused on nurturing a culture that honors the past, celebrates the present, and builds a safe, welcoming future for all. To make that vision real, we know we must listen well and recognize often. That is why this page exists. This page directly supports our strategic implementation goal to: "Create a structured plan to actively engage stakeholders by providing information and establishing opportunities for meaningful feedback."
